title: A film that could not be made in Varanasi
body: A film maker wanted to make a film about the plight of widows in Varanasi. A section of the polity protested strongly. They felt that the film would show India in a very bad light, that it was being made to cater to foreign audiences, and that it would bring a bad name to the ancient town. They refused to allow it to be made, and as a result the film could not be made in Varanasi; it was subsequently made elsewhere. Over the years several books, films and plays have similarly been banned after protests from some sections of society. Banning meets the immediate demand of the protesters, but critics argue that once a society begins to ban, it develops a habit of banning. Others point out that films are already subject to censorship, in which only a portion of a film is cut, and ask whether that is not also a kind of ban.
